company_name: Magellan Financial Group (renaming to Barrenjoey Group Limited, ASX: BJY, subject to 22 Oct 2026 AGM)
model: Operating profit after tax (FCFE) capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.fcf_basis: owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income: FY21 399.3, FY23 168.9, FY26 115.4 (A$m)
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward judgment: blended base-case revenue path (IM fee base still shrinking ~3-5%/yr for 2-3 years, Barrenjoey CF/FM growing high-single digits then converging on nominal GDP). No historical CAGR is usable: every trailing series describes the collapse of the standalone Magellan franchise after Hamish Douglass's 2022 departure, and the forward business is a different entity.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (+3.2%/+1.3%) diverges by >20pp from revenue (-23%) and EPS (-20%) CAGRs. Equity was held up by retained seed capital and the $130m March 2026 placement while the fee base halved; it is not a growth signal. Owner-FCF CAGR (-11.9% 3yr) is above reported (-11.8%) only because interest income on the cash pile grew from $1.8m to $7.1m; SBC rose from nil to $5.3m over the period.
historical_growth.notes: FUM: FY21 $113.9bn -> FY22 $61.3bn -> FY23 $39.7bn -> FY24 $36.6bn -> FY26 $36.7bn closing; average FUM FY26 $39.1bn. Average base fee 62bps (FY22) -> 52bps (FY26). Performance fees FY26 $0.1m vs $83.6m FY19.

scenario_narratives.base: FY27 is the guided transition year: operating profit after tax falls from the $215m pro forma to ~$175m (~60cps) as the heritage Global Equities funds are repriced and handed to Vinva, the seed book is de-risked into cash, legacy Barrenjoey share plans amortise and Barrenjoey NZ is set up. From FY28 Barrenjoey's Corporate Finance and Financial Markets businesses (now ~80% of revenue) grow 7-8% a year on a normal ECM/M&A cycle and the $7m cost saving plus integration synergies lift the pre-SBC margin about 1pp, while the Investment Management fee base keeps shrinking 3-4% a year (net outflows continue, base fee drifts lower, no performance fees). Group revenue compounds ~3.5% and operating profit after tax reaches ~$240m by FY36. Terminal value capped at 12x, roughly where Australian fund managers and investment banks trade through a cycle.
scenario_narratives.bull: Vinva's systematic strategies (AUM $1.7bn -> $7.6bn in FY26) and Airlie's Long/Short launch stabilise Investment Management AUM within two years; Barrenjoey compounds mid-teens off a strong ECM/M&A cycle, the NZ (Craigs) and US fixed-income build-outs pay off, and the merged platform earns operating leverage - the pre-SBC margin rebuilds to 40% (still below FY26 pro forma) and share-plan amortisation fades to 3% as legacy plans roll off. The market re-rates a diversified financial-services group (14x terminal cap) rather than a broken active manager. This needs several independent things to go right (flows, cycle, integration, talent retention), which is why it carries the lowest weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2022-26 outflow pattern continues: Global Equities and infrastructure strategies keep trailing benchmark, advisers keep redeeming, the base fee slips toward 45bps and IM revenue falls ~20% again in FY27 and keeps shrinking; a weaker Australian ECM/M&A year leaves Barrenjoey flat, so group revenue falls 6% in FY27 and barely grows thereafter. Integration frictions and talent retention (deferred-comp step-ups) keep the pre-SBC margin at 33-34% and share-plan cost at 4-4.5% of revenue. Operating profit after tax settles near $150m (~52cps), the 60-90% payout policy is used at the low end, and the terminal multiple compresses to 10x. Not a solvency case - no debt, ~$1.06bn shareholders' funds - but a value trap in which the merger dilutes rather than diversifies.

valuation_philosophy.summary: This is not a valuation of the company the historical financials describe. Magellan's core_metrics from FY15 to FY26 record the rise and collapse of a single-founder active manager: FUM peaked at $113.9bn in FY21, halved after Hamish Douglass left in 2022, and settled at $36.7bn by FY26 on a fee rate that has fallen from 62bps to 52bps; revenue fell 23% a year for five years and the flagship Global Equities funds were handed to Vinva in FY26. Peak FY21/22 earnings are not a mid-cycle anchor, and FY26 standalone is not the forward base either. On 1 July 2026 - after the FY26 balance date - MFG completed the merger with Barrenjoey, so from FY27 the reporting entity is Barrenjoey Group (~$778m pro forma revenue, three segments, ~$41bn AUM), with two-thirds of revenue transactional and cyclical rather than fee-based. The model therefore starts from FY26 PRO FORMA combined operating profit after tax ($215m), steps down to ~$175m in FY27 per management's -$33m / -11.2cps guidance plus share-plan amortisation and NZ costs, and capitalises that flow at an 11% AUD cost of equity with net debt held at zero and the balance-sheet capital treated as operating/regulatory rather than surplus. The house value is deliberately conservative on that last point (~$1.2-1.3/share of latent value if the cash proves surplus). Weighted value sits a little below the current price: the market is paying ~14x FY27 earnings for a diversified platform that has yet to prove it, and the 30% bear weight reflects that the recurring half of the business is still shrinking.
key_risks_to_valuation: Continued Investment Management outflows: $3.3bn net outflow in FY26, Global Equities AUM $13.5bn -> $3.1bn; every $1bn of AUM at ~50bps is ~$5m of revenue at near-100% incremental margin
Barrenjoey earnings cyclicality: Corporate Finance and Financial Markets revenue (ECM/DCM, M&A, trading) is market-cycle dependent and unproven through a downturn; FY26 was a strong year
Merger integration and talent retention: consolidating an asset manager and an investment bank, first consolidated accounts in FY27, deferred-compensation step-ups
FY27 guided headwinds (-$33m after tax) could prove larger if repricing triggers further redemptions or de-risking income falls faster

Pro forma base ($778m revenue / $215m operating profit) is management's figure from the results presentation, not yet an audited consolidated year; first consolidated FY27 accounts are the evidence that would move the base

Cash and seed capital (~$483m) treated as non-surplus; if the group returns it, value is higher - and if Barrenjoey's markets business consumes more capital than expected, dividends could sit at the low end of the 60-90% range

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 7.96-11.55
data_sources.financials: MFG.AX_Metrics.csv / core_metrics and kpis (FY15-FY26 annual and half-year); FY26 Annual Report (30 June 2026): segment note p.48, capital management and fund investments p.12, EPS note, Directors' Report on the Barrenjoey merger and Consideration Shares; pro forma combined FY26 revenue and operating profit per the FY26 results presentation / MFG Investor Report as summarised in MFG.AX_Analysis.json
data_sources.qualitative: MFG.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-23): business model, FY27 guidance items, bull/bear cases, recent developments

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY26 PRO FORMA combined-group revenue (MFG standalone ~$196m + Barrenjoey ~$582m), per the FY26 results presentation / MFG Investor Report cited in the Analysis JSON. The statutory FY26 revenue of $195.6m is the pre-merger standalone asset manager and is NOT the base the forward business compounds from.
inputs.share_count_basis: 185,525,496 ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 excluding treasury shares (FY26 AR p.12 fn 2) + 106,838,520 Consideration Shares issued to Barrenjoey shareholders on merger completion 1 July 2026 (FY26 AR Directors' Report) + 0.85m dilutive performance rights (diluted less basic weighted average, FY26 AR note EPS). Cross-check: management's -$33m / -11.2cps FY27 headwind implies 294.6m shares (0.5% tie). Held FLAT: share-based payments are expensed inside the operating margin (sbc_pct_path), so diluting the count as well would charge SBC twice.
inputs.cash_note: Reported cash and equivalents at 30 June 2026 were $347.9m and net fund investments $135.3m (FY26 AR p.12), with no borrowings. `cash` is set to 0 deliberately: on this route net debt is held at zero because (i) the yield on that capital (interest income $7.1m, fund investment income $40.0m pre-tax in FY26, guided to fall ~$17m after tax in FY27 as it is de-risked into cash/fixed income) stays INSIDE the capitalised operating profit, and (ii) the capital is not surplus - MAM must hold AFSL minimum NTA and from FY27 group cash is run by Barrenjoey Treasury to support the Financial Markets balance sheet. Adding the cash to EV while its income sits in the flows would count it twice. Memo: if the ~$483m of cash + fund investments were instead treated as fully surplus (income stripped, asset added at book), value would be roughly $1.2-1.3/share higher; that is the latent upside a reader should know about, not a house assumption.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY26 PRO FORMA combined-group operating profit after tax ($215m: MFG standalone $144.9m less its equity-accounted share of Barrenjoey plus Barrenjoey's $112m operating profit after tax), the flow this model capitalises. Standalone owner FCF on the house definition (reported FCF 127.8 - SBC 5.3 - interest income 7.1 = 115.4) describes the pre-merger asset manager only and is recorded in historical_growth for the CAGRs.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 AR statement of changes in equity / cash-flow reconciliation, 'Share-based payment expense' 5,325 ($'000); equity-award taxes disclosed as nil. Forward SBC is NOT this figure: FY27 guidance has employee share-plan amortisation rising to ~$20m after tax (~$28m pre-tax) as legacy Barrenjoey plans consolidate, plus MFG's ~$5m = ~$33m pre-tax, 4.3% of pro forma revenue.
inputs.buyback_note: On-market buyback $38.4m in FY26 at avg $9.70 (FY25 $74.3m). Flat count is being funded by a repurchaser, but the merger issued 106.8m shares and a 15.4m placement at $8.45, so the net count rose 58% in the year - non-SBC issuance, fully reflected in shares_outstanding.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in AUD, the currency of the flows: AU 10-year government ~4.3% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.2 for a market-sensitive funds manager / investment bank = ~11%. The same 11% is used in every scenario; cyclicality, integration and outflow risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the rate. House precedent for the route is 10% on GMG.AX/CHC.AX; +1pp here for the FY27 transition and the unproven-through-a-cycle Barrenjoey earnings.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial (lease liabilities $2.1m at 30 June 2026); lease cost is inside operating expenses, lease liabilities excluded from net debt (treatment B, trivially).
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interests: Barrenjoey is 100% owned from 1 July 2026. Vinva (28%) and FinClear (16%) remain equity-accounted associates whose profit share stays inside operating profit; their carrying value is not added to the bridge (matching-asset rule).
inputs.notes: MODEL: operating profit after tax (management's FCFE proxy, after all employee costs including share-based payments, before fair-value moves on fund investments, merger costs and intangibles amortisation) capitalised at an AUD cost of equity, net debt held at zero, through the Drivers engine: EBITDA margin is the pre-SBC pre-tax operating margin, sbc_pct_path is the share-plan charge, da/capex are zero (D&A $2.5m ~ capex, asset-light), wc_capture 0, cash tax is the blended effective rate. WHY NOT owner-FCF: standalone cash flow is dominated by seed-portfolio fair-value moves and redemptions ($235m redeemed in June 2026), and the cash pile is regulatory/operating capital for a broker-dealer, not surplus. WHY THIS BASE: the historical statements describe a pre-merger asset manager whose FUM fell from $113.9bn (FY21) to $36.7bn (FY26) - a structurally impaired, still-declining fee base (mgmt fees -13% in FY26, base fee 61bps -> 52bps, net outflows $3.3bn). The forward entity from FY27 is Barrenjoey Group: ~$778m pro forma revenue, ~$41bn AUM, three segments (Investment Management, Corporate Finance, Financial Markets), with two-thirds of revenue now transactional and cyclical. Neither peak FY21/22 earnings nor the standalone FY26 line is a base; the pro forma FY26 combined operating profit of $215m is, and FY27 steps DOWN from it per guidance. FY27 build (base): $215m - $33m guided headwind (Global Equities repricing ~$16m net of $7m savings, capital de-risking ~$17m) - ~$10m incremental share-plan amortisation - ~$5m NZ start-up + ~$8m Barrenjoey growth/synergy = ~$175m after tax (~60cps). Horizon 10 years, end-of-year discounting, terminal = min(Gordon, cap x FCF) with a 12x base cap (10x bear, 14x bull) reflecting where Australian fund managers and investment banks actually trade.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC, pre-tax operating margin on pro forma revenue. FY26 pro forma was ~39.8% (pre-tax operating profit ~$298m + ~$12m SBC on $778m). FY27 steps to 36.2% on the $30m Global Equities fee cut, ~$24m pre-tax lower investment income from de-risking and $5-10m NZ start-up costs, partly offset by $7m cost savings; recovers ~1pp over four years on integration synergies and Barrenjoey operating leverage, then flat.
base.growth_note: FY27 -2%: IM revenue ~-20% (repricing -$30m, continued outflows) against Barrenjoey +8%. Thereafter the blend is +4-4.5% while Barrenjoey (now ~80% of revenue) grows 7-8% and IM keeps shrinking 3-4%, fading to 2.5% nominal.
base.cash_tax_note: FY26 effective rate on operating profit was 21% (MFG standalone, franked dividend and offshore income). Barrenjoey is taxed at the 30% Australian rate; blend starts at 28% and drifts to 29.5% as IM shrinks in the mix.
base.sbc_note: FY27 guidance: share-plan amortisation ~$20m after tax (~$28m pre-tax) + MFG ~$5m = ~$33m, 4.3% of revenue; glides to 3.5% as legacy Barrenjoey plans roll off and are replaced by ongoing grants.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30% because the thesis rests on an unproven pivot: the recurring fee base has halved and is still shrinking, FY27 earnings are guided down, and the incoming two-thirds of revenue (Corporate Finance, Financial Markets) has never been through a down-cycle as a listed business; consensus sits at Neutral/Moderate Sell. Bull cut to 20% because it needs flows, the capital-markets cycle, integration and talent retention all to go right at once. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
